Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
Ḥā Mīm (1) The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the Wise (2) Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers (3)
Our explanation of the meaning of His saying
has already preceded. As for His saying
The revelation of the Book is from God
: its meaning is that this is the revelation of the Qurʾān from God,
in His vengeance upon His enemies,
in His management of the affair of His creation.
Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers
. He, exalted be His mention, says: Indeed, in the seven heavens, from which the rain descends, and in the earth, from which creation comes forth, O people, are
. He says: proofs and evidences for those who affirm the truth of the proofs, when they perceive and see them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
And in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain (4)
He, exalted be His mention, says: And in God's creation
of you, O people, and in His creation of what is scattered over the earth of creatures that crawl upon it, other than your kind,
are signs for a people who are certain
. He means: proofs and evidences for a people who are certain of the realities of things, so that they acknowledge them and know their soundness. The reciters differed in the reading of His saying
signs for a people who are certain
and in the one after it. Most of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read
, on the inchoative, and not linking it back to His saying
. Most of the reciters of Kufa read (āyātin) in the genitive, in the sense of the accusative, linking it back to His saying
. Those of the later authorities who read it so claim that they chose to read it thus because in Ubayy's reading, in all three verses, it is (la-āyātin) with a lām
; so they made the occurrence of the lām in his reading an indication, for them, of the soundness of reading all of it in the genitive.

But what they relied on as proof in this is no proof; for there is no sound transmission to that effect from Ubayy; and even if a transmission from Ubayy were sound, and it were then not known how he read it—in the genitive or the nominative—the judgment that he read it in the genitive would be no more fitting than the judgment that he read it in the nominative, since the Arabs sometimes insert the lām into the predicate of a word coordinated to a complete sentence on whose beginning “inna” has operated, while treating it as a fresh beginning, as Ḥumayd b. Thawr al-Hilālī said

: “Indeed, the caliphate after them is a despicable thing … and (there are) upstart successors whom I surely hold in contempt.” So he inserted the lām into the predicate of an inchoative following a predicate sentence in which “inna” had operated, since the speech, although it is begun anew, has “inna” implied in it.

The correct view in this, if the matter is as we have described, is to say: the genitive and the nominative in these words are two widespread readings among the reciters of the regions, which scholars among the reciters have read, both sound in meaning; so whichever of the two the reader reads, he is correct.

Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
These are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth; so in what statement after God and His verses will they believe? (6)
He, exalted be His mention, says: These verses and proofs, O Muḥammad, [from your Lord]
We recite to you in truth

. He says: We inform you about them with the truth, not with falsehood, as the polytheists of your people inform, falsely, about their gods, that they bring them near to God in nearness; (“so in what statement after God and His verses do you believe?”

). He, exalted be His mention, says to those who associate others with Him: So in what statement, O people, after this statement of God which He recites to you, and after His proofs against you and His evidences with which He has guided you to His oneness—that you have no lord besides Him—will you believe, if you deny His statement and His verses? This interpretation follows the reading of one who read (tuʾminūna), in the second person, as an address from God in this speech to the polytheists, and that is the reading of most of the reciters of the Kufans
As for the reading of one who read it

with yāʾ, its meaning is: So in what statement, O Muḥammad, after the statement of God which He recites to you, and these verses of His which He has drawn these polytheists' attention to and reminded them of, will these polytheists believe? That is the reading of most of the reciters of the people of Medina and Basra

. Each of the two readings has a sound aspect and an intelligible interpretation, so whichever of the two readings a reader reads, he is correct in our view, although I incline to reading it with yāʾ, since it comes in the context of verses that have preceded it in the form of report, namely His saying:
for a people who are certain

Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it; then to your Lord you will be returned (15)

He, exalted be His mention, says: Whoever among God's servants acts in obedience to Him, coming to a stop at His command and refraining at His prohibition—it is for his own soul that he did that righteous deed, and in seeking its deliverance from God's punishment that he obeyed
, and not for any other reason; for that benefits no one but him, and God is independent of the deed of every doer;
and whoever does evil, it is against it

. He says: and whoever does evil in the world, by disobeying his Lord therein and opposing His command and prohibition, it is against his own soul that he has committed a crime; for he has destroyed it by that and earned for it His wrath, and he has harmed no one
then to your Lord you will be returned

. He says: then you, O people, all of you, will go to your Lord after your death, and He will recompense the doer of good among you for his good and the evildoer for his evil; so whoever comes to Him among you with a righteous deed will be recompensed with a righteous reward, and whoever comes to Him with an evil deed will be recompensed with an evil reward.

And there will remain the nation of Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it will be said to them: What did you used to worship? They will say: We used to worship God alone, and we only separated from these in the world out of fear of this day of ours. Then the believers

will be given permission to prostrate, and the believers will prostrate, and between every believer is a hypocrite, and the back of the hypocrite will be stiff against prostration, and God will make the prostration of the believers upon him
a reproach, a humiliation, a regret and a remorse”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us,
m: , from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ b. Yazīd al-Laythī, from Abū Hurayra, he said: The people said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: “Do you suffer harm in seeing the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?” They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: “Do you suffer harm in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no cloud beneath it?” They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: “Then you will see Him on the Day of Resurrection likewise. God will gather the people and say: Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it. So whoever used to worship the moon will follow the moon, and whoever used to worship the sun will follow the sun, and whoever used to worship the ṭawāghīt will follow the ṭawāghīt; and this nation will remain among whom are its hypocrites; and their Lord will come to them in a form, and a bridge will be set over Hell.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And I will be the first to cross
, and the supplication of the messengers on that day will be: O God, deliver, O God, deliver. And on it are hooks like the thorns of the saʿdān
. Have you seen the thorns of the saʿdān?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: “They are like the thorns of the saʿdān, except that none knows
the extent of their size but God; and the people are snatched
according to their deeds; some of them are destroyed by their deed, and some are cast down
and then are saved.” Then he mentioned the ḥadīth at length

x: Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do
. He, exalted be His mention, says: Every nation will be called to its record, and it will be said to it
—that is, you will be rewarded and given the wages of what you used to do in the world of deeds; for good, good, and for evil, its recompense.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:

This is Our record, which speaks against you in truth. Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you used to do (29) So as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear attainment (30)
He, exalted be His mention, says: It will be said
to every nation called on the Resurrection to its record which it dictated to its guardians in the world:
Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do
, so do not be anxious about Our recompensing you
for that; for it speaks against you, if you deny it, with the truth; so read it.
Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you used to do

. He says: We used to have Our guardians write down your deeds, and they would record them in the books and write them. And in the like of what we have said about this the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ṭalq b. ʿAnnām told us, from Zāʾida, from ʿAṭāʾ,
m: This is Our record, which speaks against you in truth
. He said: It is the Mother of the Book, in which are the deeds of the children of Adam;
Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you used to do
. He said: Yes, the angels have the deeds of the children of Adam transcribed

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī told us, he said: My brother ʿĪsā b. ʿAbd Allāh told me,
m: , from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: God created the Nūn, which is the inkwell, and created the Pen, and said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection of deed done, whether righteous
provision apportioned, whether lawful or unlawful. Then He imposed
upon each thing of that its affair

: its entry into the world, how long its stay in it, and how its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants, and keepers over the Book; so the guardians transcribe every day from the keepers the deed of that day; and when the provision is exhausted and the trace is cut off and the term has run out, the guardians come to the keepers seeking the deed of that day, and the keepers say to them: We find nothing with us for your companion. So the guardians return [and find that they have died]
. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Are you not Arabs? You hear the guardians saying:
Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you used to do
. And can transcription be anything but from an original?
b.via: My brother ʿĪsā b. ʿAbd Allāh

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Ḥukkām told us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: This is Our record, which speaks against you in truth
. He said: The Book is the Remembrance (al-dhikr);
Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you used to do
. He said: We have the deeds transcribed.

c: And others said on this what al-Ḥasan b. ʿArafa told us, he said: al-Naḍr b. Ismāʿīl told us,
m: al-Shaybānī, from ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: God has angels who descend every day with something in which they write the deeds of the children of Adam (3).

evidence.text: He, exalted be His mention, says: It will be said (8) to every nation called on the Resurrection to its record which it dictated to its guardians in the world: {Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do}, so do not be anxious about Our recompensing you (1) for that; for it speaks against you, if you deny it, with the truth; so read it.

x: So as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy
. He, exalted be His mention, says: As for those who believed in God in the world, and affirmed His oneness, and did not associate anything with Him,
and acted by what God commanded them and refrained from what God forbade them,
their Lord will admit them into His mercy
He means: into His Paradise, by His mercy.

. He says: Their entering into God's mercy on that day is the achieving of what they sought and the attainment of what they strove for in the world—which makes plain that their end therein was that it is the attainment.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
But as for those who disbelieved: Were not My verses recited to you, but you were arrogant and were a criminal people? (31)

He, exalted be His mention, says: And as for those who denied God's oneness and refused to single Him out for divinity in the world, it will be said to them: Were not My verses recited to you in the world?
Is not “ammā” answered with the fāʾ? Where is it?
that it is the fāʾ in His saying
. The proper form of the speech in Arabic, if it were uttered in its explicit and original form, would be to say: wa-ammā alladhīna kafarū fa-a-lam

takun āyātī tutlā ʿalaykum. For the meaning of the speech is: As for those who disbelieved, it will be said to them: Were not… So the place of the fāʾ is at the beginning of the omitted part that is required in the speech; so when “it will be said” was omitted, and the interrogative alif came, whose rule is that it be put at the beginning, it was put first and the fāʾ was placed after it. The Arabs sometimes drop the fāʾ that is the answer to “ammā” in a place like this when they drop the verb that is in the position of the answer to “ammā,” as He, majestic be His praise, said:
As for those whose faces will turn black: Did you disbelieve after your belief?
[Āl ʿImrān: 106]. So the fāʾ was dropped
, since the verb in the answer of “ammā” was omitted, namely “it will be said”; for the meaning of the speech is: As for those whose faces turn black, it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve?
So when “it will be said,” to which the fāʾ is attached, was dropped, the fāʾ that is the answer to “ammā” dropped. And His saying:
. He says: but you were arrogant about listening to them and believing in them, and
. He says: and you were a people who earn
sins and disbelief in God, who do not believe in a return, nor believe in reward or punishment.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:

And when it was said: Indeed, the promise of God is true and the Hour—there is no doubt about it, you said: We do not know what the Hour is. We only assume an assumption, and we are not convinced (32)

He, exalted be His mention, says: And it will be said to them then: When it was said to you: Indeed, the promise of God, which He promised His servants, that He will give them life after their death and resurrect them from their graves, is true, and the Hour, which He told them He will establish for their gathering and their assembling for the reckoning, and for reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience, is coming
there is no doubt about it
He means: about the Hour; and the hāʾ in His saying

refers back to the mention of the Hour. And the meaning of the speech is: and the Hour—there is no doubt about its coming; so fear God and believe in God and His Messenger, and work for what will save you from God's punishment therein—
you said: We do not know what the Hour is
, in denial on your part of the promise of God, majestic be His praise, and rejection of His report, and denial of His power to give you life after your death.
. [He says: and you said: We do not think the Hour is coming except as an assumption]
that it is coming, nor that it will come to be. The reciters differed in the reading of His saying:
and the Hour—there is no doubt about it
. Most of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read
in the nominative as an inchoative
. And most of the reciters of Kufa read (wa-l-sāʿata) in the accusative
Indeed, the promise of God is true

. The correct view on this in our opinion is that they are two widespread readings among the reciters of the regions, both sound in derivation in Arabic and close in meaning; so whichever of the two the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of His saying: {and the Hour—there is no doubt about it}.
Most of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read {wa-l-sāʿatu} in the nominative as an inchoative (1).
And most of the reciters of Kufa read (wa-l-sāʿata) in the accusative (2), coordinating it to His saying {Indeed, the promise of God is true}.

The correct view on this in our opinion is that they are two widespread readings among the reciters of the regions, both sound in derivation in Arabic and close in meaning; so whichever of the two the reader reads, he is correct.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
And there will appear to them the evils of what they did, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule (33)

He, exalted be His mention, says: And there will appear to these who used to disbelieve in God's verses in the world the evils of what they did of deeds in the world. He says: their ugliness and wickedness will appear to them there, when they read the books of their deeds which the guardians used to transcribe in the world;
and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule
. He says: and there will encompass them of God's punishment then that which they used to ridicule, when it was said to them that God would inflict it upon whoever
denied Him, for the evils of the deeds they did in the world.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
And it will be said: Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers (34)

He, exalted be His mention, says: And it will be said to these disbelievers whose description He described: Today We leave you in the punishment of Hell, as you left deeds for the meeting with your Lord on this Day of yours.

c: As ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās

x: and your refuge is the Fire
. He says: and your refuge [to which you take refuge] is the Fire of Hell,
and you will have no helpers
. He says: and you have no rescuer who will rescue you
today from God's punishment, nor any supporter who will support you against the one who punishes you, [so as to rescue you]
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
That is because you took the verses of God in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be asked to appease (35)

He, exalted be His mention, says: It will be said to them: This which has befallen you of God's punishment today is because you in the world took God's verses in mockery. They are His proofs and evidences and the verses of His Book which He sent down upon His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace,
. He means: in ridicule with which you ridiculed them;
and the worldly life deceived you
. He says: and the adornment of the worldly life deluded you, so you preferred it over acting by what
would save you today from God's punishment. He, exalted be His mention, says:
so today they will not be brought out of it
nor will they be asked to appease
. He says: nor will they be returned to the world to repent and return in penitence from what they were punished for.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
So to God belongs [all] praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds (36) And to Him belongs greatness in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the Wise

He, exalted be His mention, says: So to God belongs praise for His favors and benefactions to His creation; so praise Him, O people, for every favor you have is from Him, not from what you worship besides Him of gods and idols, nor from what you take
besides Him as a lord and associate with Him
Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth
. He says: Owner of the seven heavens and Owner of the seven earths
. He says: Owner of all that is in them of kinds of creation.
And to Him belongs greatness in the heavens and the earth
. He says: and to Him belong magnificence and sovereignty in the heavens and the earth, to the exclusion of all other gods and rivals,
in His vengeance upon His enemies, the Subduer of all that is beneath Him, whom nothing subdues,
in His management of His creation and His directing them as He wishes, however He wishes. And God knows best. End of the commentary on Sūrat “al-Jāthiya.”

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 212 عن معمر، عن قتادة نحوه.

notes.en: It is an irregular (shādhdh) reading. Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ 8/49: ʿAbd Allāh read “illā dahrun,” and its interpretation is: except a time that passes. See Mukhtaṣar al-Shawādhdh by Ibn Khālawayh, p. 139.
notes.ar: وهى قراءة شاذة، قال أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 8/ 49 وقرأ عبد الله "إلا دهر" وتأويله: إلا دهر يمر. وينظر مختصر الشواذ لابن خالويه ص 139.

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 600; and al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/35 attributes it to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 600، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 35 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Reported by ʿAbd al-Razzāq in his Tafsīr 2/212, from Maʿmar, with it.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 212 عن معمر به.

notes.en: In T2 and T3: “whoever said that.”
After it in M and T1: “and.”

Reported by al-Dāraquṭnī in al-ʿIlal 8/81, via Sufyān, with it; and the statement “The people of the Jāhiliyya used to say … so they would curse time” is mawqūf (a statement of Sufyān), as in Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Ḥibbān (5715) and al-Mustadrak 2/453; and the marfūʿ part of it was reported by al-Ḥumaydī (1096), Aḥmad 12/187 (7245), al-Bukhārī (4826), Muslim (2/2246), Abū Dāwūd (5274), al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11487), Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as in Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr 7/254—and al-Bayhaqī 3/365, via Sufyān with it.
notes.ar:
أخرجه الدارقطني في العلل 8/ 81 من طريق سفيان به، وقوله: "كان أهل الجاهلية 
…. فيسبون الدهر". موقوف على سفيان كما في صحيح ابن حبان (5715)، والمستدرك 2/ 453، وأخرج المرفوع منه الحميدى (1096)، وأحمد 12/ 187 (7245)، والبخارى (4826)، ومسلم (2/ 2246)، وأبو داود (5274)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11487)، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 7/ 254 - والبيهقى 3/ 365 من طريق سفيان به.

notes.en: Reported by Muslim (2246/1), al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11486) and al-Bayhaqī 3/365 via Ibn Wahb with it; and al-Bukhārī (6181) reported it via Yūnus b. Yazīd with it.
notes.ar: أخرجه مسلم (2246/ 1)، والنسائى في الكبرى (11486)، والبيهقى 365/ 3 من طريق ابن وهب به، وأخرجه البخارى (6181) من طريق يونس بن يزيد به.

notes.en: Reported by Aḥmad 13/368 (7988), al-Bukhārī in Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād (343), Ibn Khuzayma (2479) and al-Ḥākim 1/418 via Ibn Isḥāq with it; and Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunna (598) reported it via al-ʿAlāʾ in abridged form.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 13/ 368 (7988)، والبخارى في خلق أفعال العباد (343)، وابن خزيمة (2479)، والحاكم 1/ 418 من طريق ابن إسحاق به، وأخرجه ابن أبي عاصم في السنة (598) من طريق العلاء به مختصرا.

notes.en: After it in the manuscripts: “from Qatāda.” See the sources of the takhrīj.
notes.ar: بعده في النسخ: "عن قتادة". وينظر مصدر التخريج.

notes.en: Reported by ʿAbd al-Razzāq in his Tafsīr 2/212, from Maʿmar, with it.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 212 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Omitted from the manuscripts; what is given is as has preceded at 10/596, and it is so in the source of the takhrīj.
notes.ar: سقط من النسخ، والمثبت كما تقدم في 10/ 596، وهو كذلك في مصدر التخريج.

notes.en: Reported by Muslim (2246/5) via Jarīr, from Hishām, from Muḥammad b. Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
notes.ar: أخرجه مسلم (2246/ 5) من طريق جرير، عن هشام، عن محمد بن سيرين، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

notes.en: In T1: “to them”; omitted from T2 and T3.
notes.ar: في ت 1: "لهم"، وسقط من: ت 2، ت 3.

notes.en: After it in T2 and T3: “if you are truthful, that is.”
notes.ar: بعده في ت 2، ت 3: "إن كنتم صادقين أي".

notes.en: After it in T2: “from the truthful, if you are,” and in T3: “from the truthful, that you were.”
notes.ar: بعده في ت:2: "من الصادقين إن كنت"، وفى ت 3: "من الصادقين أي كنت".

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, T2 and T3: “min.”
In Ṣ, T1, T2 and T3: “alladhīna.”
In Ṣ, T1, T2 and T3: “manāzilahum.”
Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 600, and via it al-Firyābī—as in Taghlīq al-Taʿlīq 4/311; and al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/36 attributes it to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 600، ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 311، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 36 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/36 attributes it to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 36 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: In T2 and T3: “li-l-muʾmin” (for the believer).
Al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/36 attributes it to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 36 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: After it in the manuscripts: “from Qatāda.” See the sources of the takhrīj.
notes.ar: بعده في النسخ: "عن قتادة"، وينظر مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: Al-saʿdān: a thorny plant, one of the best pastures for camels, on which they grow fat. al-Nihāya 2/367.
notes.ar: السعدان: نبت ذو شوك، وهو من جيِّد مراعى الإبل تسمن عليه. النهاية 2/ 367.

notes.en: Al-mukhardal: one thrown down and cast aside; and it is said: one cut to pieces, cut by the hooks of the Ṣirāṭ until he falls into the Fire. Lisān (kh-r-d-l).
notes.ar: المخردل: المصروع المرميّ، وقيل: المقطع تقطِّعه كلاليب الصراط حتى يهوِى في النار. اللسان (خردل).

notes.en: Reported by al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11637) from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā with it; and Ibn Mandah in al-Īmān (806) and al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿa (598) via Ibn Thawr in abridged form; and Maʿmar reported it in his Jāmiʿ (20856), and via him Aḥmad 13/143–146 (7717), al-Bukhārī (6573), Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim (455) and Ibn Ḥibbān (7429).
notes.ar: أخرجه النسائي في الكبرى (11637) عن محمد بن عبد الأعلى به، وابن منده في الإيمان (806)، والآجرى في الشريعة (598) من طريق ابن ثور به مختصرًا، وأخرجه معمر في جامعه (20856) ومن طريقه أحمد 13/ 143 - 146 (7717)، والبخارى (6573)، وابن أبي عاصم (455)، وابن حبان (7429).

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, pp. 600–601, via ʿAṭāʾ with it.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 600، 601 من طريق عطاء به.

notes.en: In Ṣ: “shāmahu”; in T2: “sāma”; and in T3: “sāmahu.”
notes.ar: في ص: "شامه"، وفى ت 2: "سامة"، وفي ت 3: "سامه".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/36 attributes it to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 36 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, T2 and T3: “la-ātiya.”
Omitted from: T1, T2 and T3.
It is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. See al-Sabʿa by Ibn Mujāhid, p. 595.
notes.ar: هي قراءة نافع وابن كثير وأبي عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي. ينظر السبعة لابن مجاهد ص 595.

notes.en: It is the reading of Ḥamza. Ibid.
After it in T2: “in God's punishment.”

= And the report is attributed by al-Ḥāfiẓ in al-Fatḥ 8/574 to Ibn al-Mundhir, and by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/37 to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. [This is the continuation of a note from the preceding unit, which the source dataset places here.]
notes.ar: = والأثر عزاه الحافظ في الفتح 8/ 574 إلى ابن المنذر، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 37 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: After it in Ṣ and M: “and.”
